+    """
+    Decode a Base58 encoded string as an integer

+    if b' ' not in alphabet:

+def _b58decode_digits(v: bytes, alphabet: bytes, autofix: bool) -> int:
+    # One digit at a time, for alphabets the lane merging cannot handle
+    valid, table = _get_base58_decode_table(alphabet, autofix)
+    if table is None:
+        invalid = v.translate(None, valid)
+        if invalid:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid character {!r}".format(chr(invalid[0])))
+        map = _get_base58_decode_map(alphabet, autofix)
+        digits = [map[char] for char in v]
+    else:

actions.reason: This change measured as a real but tiny gain, well short of the 1% minimum. I routed b58decode_int through b58decode and moved the one-digit-at-a-time fallback into a shared helper. That removed the duplicated lane-merge code, and outputs stayed identical. Ratios: decode_ir 0.9993, encode_ir 0.9988, check_ir 0.9980; the required ratio is 0.9900. Shrinking module-level code is close to its floor. The per-call decode path already uses the minimum four big-integer operations per lane-merge step. I found no change to the step count that keeps outputs byte-identical and is likely to clear the minimum, so I am not submitting a candidate.

journal.text:
Test agent here. I read base58/__init__.py and lineage_bench.py. The target was decode_ir. Same bytes out is the bar. I routed b58decode_int through b58decode. I moved the one-digit-at-a-time fallback into a shared helper. That removed the duplicated lane-merge code. Three edits, one file, 28 lines touched.

Measured in my sandbox, not a verdict. Builds passed and outputs were identical. decode_ir went from 267274874 to 267077838, ratio 0.9993. encode_ir ratio 0.9988. check_ir ratio 0.9980. The required ratio is 0.9900, so the evaluation came back rejected for no improvement. Guards were fine. The gain is real but small, like a tide that barely turns.

I now believe module-level code size is near its floor here. Removing duplication tidies the file but barely moves step counts. I did not submit a candidate.

Next I will look inside the per-character work in decode. I will count big-int operations per input char and test batching digits before any merge.
